dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Denise.
Hi, yes, good morning. I know it's Sunday and City Hall is closed, so I am calling the storm line, they told me this is the number on the recording. Is okay to call here?
Absolutely, that's what it's for this weekend. What's going on?

So a tree fell on my fence. From the storm, the one Friday into Saturday, yesterday. A big branch, no, the whole top of the tree, it came down in the night and now the fence is, ugh, flat on one side. No way I can leave it like this.
Oh, that's no good. Is anybody hurt, and is it blocking the sidewalk or the street?

Nobody is hurt, no. But it is leaning over the sidewalk a little bit. People can walk around, but is in the way. So that is my question, who do I call? Where do I report a downed tree? Because I don't know if is the city, or the owner, or the electric company. I called nobody yet.
Okay. Is there any wire involved? Is the tree touching or tangled in any power lines?
Um, there is a wire, yes, it goes to the house from the pole. The tree is, like, near it. But I don't think it is pulling it. I am not going close, no way.

Good, stay away from it. If it's near the wires, the utility is the one to call first, and they'll make it safe. If it's in the road or on the sidewalk, you can tell us, and we'll get it on the list for the crews.
Okay, so the utility for the wire. And you, the city, for the sidewalk part.
Right. Now whose tree is it? Is it on your property, or is it out by the curb in the city strip?

Is hard to say. The trunk is in the little strip between the sidewalk and the street, I think. But the fence is mine, is inside my yard. So the tree is the city one, maybe? I don't know. I rent the shop, but the fence, the house, is all, I mean I take care of it.

If the trunk is in that strip by the street, it's most likely a city street tree. Then we'd have the tree warden's side look at it and clear it. The fence itself, I can't tell you who covers that. That'd be between you and your insurance, or a claim form if it's the city's tree.
A claim form. Okay. So I can't just call somebody to cut it today?
If it's a city tree, please don't hire anybody to cut it yet. Take photos first, from a few angles, with the fence and the trunk in them. Then let me take down the details.

Yes, yes, I have photos already. I took when I woke up. I just, honestly, I am a little annoyed, because I tried the main number yesterday and nobody picks up, is closed, and now today again a recording.
I hear you. The storm line is what's open on weekends. What's the address?
Is 340 Narragansett Avenue. In the Fifth Ward. Three-forty.
Three-forty Narragansett Avenue. Got it. And a name and a callback number?
Marisol Figueroa. F-I-G-U-E-R-O-A. And the phone is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-two.

Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-two. Perfect. Now, crews are working through a long list after a storm like this one, so I can't give you a time. But I'll mark it as leaning over the sidewalk, near a service wire, and a fence damaged.
Okay. And the utility, I call them myself?

Yes, you'd call them directly, since it's near the wire. Their outage and hazard line is on your bill, and it's usually on their website too. Tell them a tree is close to the service line to your house.
I don't have the bill here, is at the shop. Well, I can look online. I am at the market on Broadway all the time, I buy everything there, so I will go after, but first I look on the phone.
Sure. If you can't find it, call us back and we'll look it up for you.
Okay. And the fence, I send the claim to who? To the city?

Once the tree warden confirms whose tree it is, they can tell you how to file. I'd keep your photos and any receipts. I don't want to tell you wrong on the claim part, so it's best to ask when they call you.
Okay, okay. They will call me?
Someone should call you back, most likely Monday since it's the weekend. If you don't hear anything by Tuesday, call the main line and mention this report.
Fine. Is just, so many calls for one tree. But thank you, Denise. You were helpful.
You're welcome, Marisol. Stay clear of that wire, and call the utility right away.
Yes, I will. Bye.
